what_happened: Scene layout 5 (black cabinets, black dishwasher door, robot right of the dishwasher), white cup_5 and dark bowl_6. Stage 0: bowl grasped 221 (re-close 233), carried to the slid-out rack and released 340; stage 0 complete 343 (normal). Stage 1: cup grasped 463-474 by the rim so it hung sideways, carried over the rack and released 637 lying on its side (tilt 90 deg for the rest of the episode); stage 1 complete 652 (309 steps, a bit above p90 272). Stage 2: 664-768 the gripper went to the left end of the rack and pushed it back into the tub (rack in by ~800, dishwasher touch 747-765). 832-904 it went down to the outer tip of the open door and from 911 to 1200 stayed there in contact with the door (touch 911-1200), with almost no visible motion. The door closedness peaked at 0.08 (960) and 0.06 (1072) and was 0.00 at the end. In the wrist view the door is a black band in front of/below the fingers with the rack beyond it; in successful closes (s12 740, s7 596, s29 772, s24 816) the wrist is filled by the door underside because the fingers are under the door lifting it.
causal_chain: both dishes on the rack by 652 (548 steps left; stage 2 median 169, p90 273) -> rack pushed in 700-800 (correct) -> gripper parked at the door's outer tip 832-1200 without getting under it -> door rose at most 0.08 -> door open at timeout
self_recovery: none effective: 290 steps of contact at the same spot; small lifts to 0.08 and 0.06 fell back each time. It never repositioned under the door or tried another part of it.
official_criterion_notes: The cup lies on its side on the rack from 637 and still counts as placed (rack contact only, no upright test). fixtures.stage2 touch 591-644 is the gripper brushing the rack/door while placing the cup, not a close attempt.
uncertain_about: Why the door does not lift: from the 4-step 256-px frames I cannot tell whether the fingers press against the door's front lip, sit just beyond it, or the arm is at its reach limit near the floor. The same layout (s6) did lift the door to 0.26 once.
